stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured $88 million in funding from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
The company is rapidly gaining traction, currently serving 8.9 million developers.
The funding validates the growing importance and adoption of open-source large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 introduces significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It integrates built-in support for Ollama, leveraging existing local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in preview, indicating early adoption of Apple's ML framework.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy.
The core value proposition is connecting messaging workflows directly to local AI capabilities.

stories.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum error correction is being advanced by using reinforcement learning.
The core mechanism involves using error information to dynamically adjust control algorithms.
This development represents a significant step toward building stable and functional quantum processors.

stories.title: Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A ransomware negotiator was arrested for betraying his clients.
The individual was found to be working in collusion with the ransomware attackers.
The case resulted in a six-year prison sentence for the negotiator.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video.
Addresses a critical gap in current research: reliably evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for reasoning about safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving understanding.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Current LLM evaluation (accuracy/perplexity) is insufficient for assessing quantization effects.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to measure behavioral changes post-quantization.
This research addresses a critical deployment challenge by providing a more robust evaluation method for resource-constrained LLMs.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: Introduces ARDY, a new model combining Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for human motion generation.
Addresses the critical gap between high-quality, controllable offline motion generation and the low inference speed needed for real-time interactive applications.
Aims to enable realistic, controllable 3D human motion synthesis suitable for robotics, animation, and simulation.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—parameters whose removal drastically degrades model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weight-aware training improves performance, showing isolation training leads to accuracy collapse.
Demonstrates that the concept of critical Super Weights is not universally applicable across all Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents.
Addresses limitations of existing benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluations.
Aims to provide a more rigorous evaluation framework for real-world, multi-capability agent tasks.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to overcome limitations in current LLM-based web search.
It addresses the constraint of single ReAct agents being limited by trajectory length and context window when handling complex, deep-and-wide research tasks.
The system aims to improve upon existing multi-agent methods by specifically enhancing recursive search depth and coverage.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches physical limits for LLMs.
Proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
Aims to overcome limitations of existing refinement techniques (rule-based and LLM-based) regarding quality and efficiency.

stories.title: Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius: Inside the Circular Financing of the GPU Boom
stories.author: adletbalzhanov
bullet_points: The article discusses the complex financial dynamics fueling the current GPU boom.
It focuses on the circular financing models involving major players like Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius.
This suggests a deep dive into the infrastructure and capital flow supporting the AI hardware shortage.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update expands model support across various hardware, complementing the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM deployment via Ollama for more complex tasks.

stories.title: China recovered its first reusable rocket and showed a new way to do it
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: China has successfully recovered its first reusable rocket.
The recovery demonstrated a new methodology for achieving reusability.
The effort is noted as an attempt to replicate successful technologies pioneered by SpaceX.

stories.title: Firmware update bricks Hue Bridge Pro devices; Philips gives free replacements
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A firmware update has caused Hue Bridge Pro devices to become inoperable (bricked).
Philips is providing free replacement units to affected customers.
Users will need to reconfigure all their associated lighting setups and settings.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces 'OpenCoF,' a new approach to enabling reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes 'Chain-of-Frame (CoF)' reasoning as a temporal alternative to traditional Chain-of-Thought (CoT) in video.
Addresses the limitation of current video generators, which lack specific supervision for robust CoF reasoning.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to reason about the lineage of scientific ideas.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific innovation as an inheritance process, similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on benchmarking 'lineage reasoning' and 'lineage-grounded idea generation' in scientific contexts.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and degree.
The research addresses a gap in existing literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported data to examine actual usage behavior.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research focuses on leveraging the internal kNN graph constructed by UMAP, rather than just its final low-dimensional embedding.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, avoiding projection distortion.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this graph enhances data sensemaking capabilities beyond typical UMAP usage.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: The paper introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The research highlights a critical distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity when using LLMs for inferring complex theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight plug-in temporal transformer, named BioModule, is proposed to bridge pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The work has relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that low error in forward diffusion marginals guarantees numerical stability in sampling.
It demonstrates that a smooth score field with small forward-marginal error can still lead to a non-explosive, stable reverse-time process.
The research highlights a crucial distinction between average error metrics (forward marginals) and trajectory-specific stability (discretized reverse-time sampling).

stories.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
stories.author: Shiwei Liu
bullet_points: SLORR introduces a new low-rank regularization technique designed to improve neural network compressibility.
It addresses limitations of existing methods, such as the need for SVDs of large matrices or architectural modifications.
The proposed method is highlighted as being simple, stateless, and efficient during the training process.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research focuses on leveraging the internal k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed by UMAP, rather than just its final low-dimensional embedding.
This internal graph preserves the structure of the high-dimensional data manifold before projection distortion occurs.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this graph enhances data sensemaking capabilities, suggesting a new avenue for UMAP utilization.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has high relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring flexible, language-based reasoning capabilities from LLMs to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing Autoregressive Variational Inference to organize information for control.
Aims to bridge the gap between high-level linguistic reasoning and low-level, granular spatial/motor control.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model designed for wildfire-prone landscapes.
Addresses the limitations of current methods (expensive LiDAR vs. sparse image-based reconstruction) for large areas.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to improve terrain mapping accuracy for emergency response.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The model shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like measuring the moral foundation of authority.
The research highlights the critical distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity when using LLMs for complex theoretical annotation.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where crucial information gets lost in growing trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for agents.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface and utilize scattered, decision-relevant state information over long periods.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper investigates the necessity and capability of using large language models (LLMs) as judges/reward models for citation verification in deep-research systems.
It addresses the critical calibration question: how capable and unbiased must an LLM judge be when verifying the quality of source attribution.
The study focuses on citation quality as a structured rubric task, essential for ensuring search-grounded LLMs support all claims with cited sources.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces DominoTree, a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding.
Addresses a limitation in existing block-diffusion drafters (like DFlash) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction.
Allows the draft token distribution to be path-dependent, overcoming the factorized limitations of methods like DDTree.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: The study addresses a critical gap in health AI by analyzing real patient-chatbot conversations, moving beyond simulated data.
It highlights the significant variability in communication patterns and emotional expression among real users interacting with LLM-powered chatbots.
The researchers developed a sophisticated patient simulator capable of modeling clinical content, emotional state, and conversational strategy.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks consume excessive memory.
Proposes MAESTRO, a new method to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
Distinguishes itself from existing pruning methods by accounting for the interdependent nature of MoE routing, unlike dense transformer methods.

stories.title: Show HN: Mindwalk – Replay coding-agent sessions on a 3D map of your codebase
stories.author: cosmtrek
bullet_points: Introduces 'Mindwalk,' a tool designed to replay coding-agent sessions.
The core innovation is visualizing these sessions on an interactive 3D map of the codebase.
This addresses the challenge of understanding complex, multi-step AI agent interactions within large codebases.

stories.title: How to Stop AI Agent Cost Blowups Before They Happen
stories.author: sapph1re
bullet_points: Addresses a critical, practical problem: preventing runaway costs in multi-agent AI systems.
Provides actionable solutions like budget guards and circuit breakers for cost control.
Offers framework-specific guidance for popular orchestration tools (CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph).

stories.title: How I Made the Cheapest Model Match the Best — at 1/640th the Cost
stories.author: matthew_lancaster_bb61910
bullet_points: The article details a method to achieve high-quality results using a significantly cheaper LLM (Claude Haiku).
The core innovation involves building a custom memory system to enhance the performance of the budget model.
This work addresses the cost-efficiency challenge in deploying powerful AI models.

stories.title: 🔁 Stop Running Opus for Everything: Loop Engineering and the Multi-Model Playbook in Claude Code
stories.author: suraj_khaitan_f893c243958
bullet_points: The article suggests that the key advantage in Claude Code is not model size or prompting, but rather implementing 'loops'.
It advocates for a 'Multi-Model Playbook' approach when utilizing Claude Code.
This indicates a shift in best practices from monolithic prompting to iterative, multi-stage engineering workflows.
